parts.text: Which claim correctly says whether a new substance has formed?

options.text: The nail’s brown coat is a new substance (chemical change); melting ice is not a new substance (physical change).
Melting ice forms a new substance (chemical change); the nail’s brown coat does not (physical change).
Both changes form a new substance because both look different afterward.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Firoz watches two changes. An iron nail left in damp air gets a brown flaky coat. Ice melts in a glass.

part_answers.answer: Rust is a new substance, so that change is chemical; ice and water are the same substance, so melting is physical.

teacher.key_rationale: A chemical change forms a new substance (rust on the nail). Melting ice does not form a new substance, so it is physical.
